Repository: /luxon — the JavaScript library 'luxon' v1.20.0. Source in /luxon/src, tests in /luxon/test, jest. Fix this reported bug:

BUG: With `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true`, `Interval.fromISO("2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00/PT5H30M")` throws `InvalidArgumentError: Invalid DateTime` instead of returning the valid interval (the same interval you get when throwOnInvalid is left at its default false). The same happens with the duration first: `Interval.fromISO("PT5H30M/2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00")`. Both halves of the string are individually valid and parse fine on their own.

Expected behavior (from the repo's own docs): `Interval.fromISO` accepts `<start>/<end>`, `<start>/<duration>`, and `<duration>/<end>` formats (see the docstring on Interval.fromISO in src/interval.js) and should return the interval regardless of the throwOnInvalid setting.

Your task:
1. First run the full test suite to record pre-existing failures: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -60`.
2. Read /luxon/src/interval.js (static fromISO) and /luxon/src/datetime.js (static fromISO) and /luxon/src/duration.js (static fromISO) and /luxon/src/settings.js to find the root cause. Likely cause: Interval.fromISO calls `DateTime.fromISO` on the duration half of the string; when throwOnInvalid is true that throws instead of returning an invalid DateTime, so the duration branch is never reached. Fix it minimally in src/interval.js (do not change public API or other behavior).
3. Verify your fix with a scratch script (e.g. write /luxon/scratch_check.js, run `cd /luxon && npx babel-node scratch_check.js`, then DELETE it). Verify: with Settings.throwOnInvalid = true, both `Interval.fromISO("2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00/PT5H30M")` and `Interval.fromISO("PT5H30M/2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00")` return valid intervals equal to what you get with throwOnInvalid false; also check start/end ISO strings, and that a genuinely unparsable interval still behaves as before (returns an invalid Interval, or throws consistently with throwOnInvalid semantics).
4. Re-run the full test suite and compare failures to the baseline.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: do NOT modify or delete any existing test file; do not break any pre-existing passing test; do not add features. Report back: the root cause, the exact diff you made, before/after test failures, and the verification output.

Repository: /luxon — the JavaScript library 'luxon' v1.20.0. Source in /luxon/src, tests in /luxon/test, jest. Fix this reported bug:

BUG: `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 61 }).toISODate()` returns "0100-03-01" but should return "0100-03-02". Adding 61 days to 0099-12-31 must land on 0100-03-02 (Dec 31 + 31 = Jan 31, + 28 (year 100 is NOT a leap year) = Feb 28, + 2 = Mar 2). The bug appears when the addition crosses the year-100 boundary and passes through February.

Your task:
1. First run the full test suite to record pre-existing failures: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -60`.
2. Investigate. Strong hint: look at `objToLocalTS` in /luxon/src/impl/util.js. It calls Date.UTC(obj.year, ...) and then, for years 0..99, does `d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)` to undo the legacy 19XX mapping. Because Date.UTC maps year 99 to 1999 and the day may overflow into the next year, the intermediate date can land in a leap year (2000) while the target year (100) is not a leap year, shifting the result by one day. Fix it so that the year/month/day are all re-applied together (e.g. `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`), preserving correct behavior for all other inputs. Make sure the fix handles years 0..99 correctly including day overflow and leap-year differences.
3. Verify with a scratch script (write /luxon/scratch_check.js, run `cd /luxon && npx babel-node scratch_check.js`, then DELETE it). Check at least: DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({day:61}).toISODate() === "0100-03-02"; DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({day:1}).toISODate() === "0100-01-01"; DateTime.fromISO("0001-01-01", {zone:"UTC"}).toISODate() === "0001-01-01"; DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({day:60}).toISODate() === "0100-03-01"; also a normal year case like DateTime.fromISO("2020-01-31").plus({day:1}).toISODate() === "2020-02-01". Also run a few round trips for years 0001..0100.
4. Re-run the full test suite and compare failures to the baseline.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: do NOT modify or delete any existing test file; do not break any pre-existing passing test; do not add features. Report back: the root cause, the exact diff, before/after test failures, and verification output.

Repository: /luxon — the JavaScript library 'luxon' v1.20.0. Source in /luxon/src, tests in /luxon/test, jest (run `cd /luxon && npx jest`). Fix this reported bug:

BUG: A FixedOffsetZone constructed from a non-numeric offset is accepted as a valid zone instead of being rejected:
```js
const { DateTime, FixedOffsetZone } = require("luxon");
const zone = new FixedOffsetZone("CDT");
console.log(zone.isValid); // true, but expected false
const dt = DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone });
console.log(dt.isValid, dt.invalidReason); // true undefined, but expected false "unsupported zone"
```
Expected: `new FixedOffsetZone("CDT").isValid === false`, and any DateTime created with such a zone is invalid with invalidReason "unsupported zone".

Your task:
1. First run the full test suite to record pre-existing failures: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -60`. (Known pre-existing failures: 2 tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js about French locale hour padding — ignore those.)
2. Investigate /luxon/src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js, /luxon/src/zone.js (base class `isValid`), /luxon/src/impl/zoneUtil.js (`normalizeZone`), and how DateTime validates its zone (search for `unsupported zone` in /luxon/src/datetime.js). Fix minimally so a FixedOffsetZone whose offset is not a number reports isValid === false and DateTimes built with it are invalid with reason "unsupported zone". Make sure `zone.name` / `zone.offset()` / `zone.formatOffset()` do not throw for such an invalid zone (the error message uses zone.name). Do NOT change behavior for valid numeric offsets, for UTC, or for FixedOffsetZone.parseSpecifier.
3. Verify with a scratch script (write /luxon/scratch_check_zone.js, run `cd /luxon && npx babel-node scratch_check_zone.js`, then DELETE it). Check at least: `new FixedOffsetZone("CDT").isValid === false`; `DateTime.fromMillis(0, {zone: new FixedOffsetZone("CDT")}).isValid === false` with invalidReason "unsupported zone"; `new FixedOffsetZone(60).isValid === true` and DateTime with it is valid with offset 60; `FixedOffsetZone.utcInstance.isValid === true`; `FixedOffsetZone.parseSpecifier("UTC+6")` still works; `DateTime.fromMillis(0,{zone:"UTC+5:30"})` still valid; also `DateTime.fromMillis(0,{zone: new FixedOffsetZone(undefined)}).isValid === false` and `new FixedOffsetZone(null).isValid === false`.
4. Re-run the full test suite and compare failures to the baseline.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: do NOT modify or delete any existing test file; do not break any pre-existing passing test; do not add features. Report back: root cause, exact diff, before/after test failures, verification output.

Repository: /luxon — the JavaScript library 'luxon' v1.20.0. Source in /luxon/src, tests in /luxon/test, jest (run `cd /luxon && npx jest`). Fix this reported bug:

BUG: formatting ISO dates for negative (BCE) years mangles the year because the minus sign is counted as a digit when zero-padding:
```js
DateTime.fromObject({ year: -1, month: 1, day: 1, zone: "utc" }).toISODate();
// expected "-0001-01-01", got "00-1-01-01"

DateTime.fromObject({ year: -10, month: 1, day: 1, zone: "utc" }).toISODate();
// expected "-0010-01-01", got "00-10-01-01"
```
Positive years pad correctly; only years before 1 CE are wrong.

Your task:
1. First run the full test suite to record pre-existing failures: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -60`. (Known pre-existing failures: 2 tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js about French locale hour padding — ignore those.)
2. Investigate. Likely culprit: `padStart` in /luxon/src/impl/util.js, which does `("0".repeat(n) + input).slice(-n)` and therefore counts a leading '-' as a digit. It is used by the year token formatting in /luxon/src/impl/formatter.js (search for `padStart` and for the 'yyyy'/'yy' tokens). Fix so that negative years render as `-0001` (i.e. the sign is emitted separately and the absolute value is zero-padded to the requested width). Be careful: `padStart` is also used for offsets and other numeric fields — make sure non-negative inputs and existing behavior are unchanged, and that the `yyyy`/`yy`/`y` tokens and toISODate/toISO/toFormat all behave. Also check `DateTime.fromObject({year:-1,...}).toISO()` and `.toFormat("yyyy-MM-dd")`.
3. Verify with a scratch script (write /luxon/scratch_check_year.js, run `cd /luxon && npx babel-node scratch_check_year.js`, then DELETE it). Check at least: year -1 -> "-0001-01-01"; year -10 -> "-0010-01-01"; year -12345 -> "-12345-01-01"; year 1 -> "0001-01-01"; year 2020 -> "2020-01-01"; and that offsets still format correctly (e.g. DateTime.fromObject({year:2020,month:1,day:1,zone:"UTC+5:30"}).toISO() === "2020-01-01T00:00:00.000+05:30"). Also check toFormat("yyyy-MM-dd") for those years.
4. Re-run the full test suite and compare failures to the baseline.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: do NOT modify or delete any existing test file; do not break any pre-existing passing test; do not add features. Report back: root cause, exact diff, before/after test failures, verification output.

Repository: /luxon — the JavaScript library 'luxon' v1.20.0. Source in /luxon/src, tests in /luxon/test, jest. Fix this reported bug:

BUG: `DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-06", { zone: "America/Los_Angeles" }).isInDST` returns false, but should return true — in 1974 US daylight saving time started on January 6. The same date in a normal year reports correctly.

Your task:
1. First run the full test suite to record pre-existing failures: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -60`.
2. Investigate. The getter `isInDST` is in /luxon/src/datetime.js (~line 1164). It currently compares `this.offset` against `this.set({ month: 1 }).offset` and `this.set({ month: 5 }).offset`, assuming January is always standard time and May is always DST. In 1974 January 6 was already DST, so `this.set({ month: 1 })` keeps the same date and the comparison fails. Fix it so that 1974-01-06 in America/Los_Angeles reports isInDST === true, while keeping all existing behavior/tests intact (e.g. compare against `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 })` so the January reference point is January 1, which was standard time in 1974). Think carefully about southern-hemisphere zones and fixed-offset zones, and about invalid DateTimes (isInDST must stay falsy for invalid DateTimes).
3. Verify with a scratch script (write /luxon/scratch_check.js, run `cd /luxon && npx babel-node scratch_check.js`, then DELETE it). Check at least: DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-06",{zone:"America/Los_Angeles"}).isInDST === true; DateTime.fromISO("1974-01-05",{zone:"America/Los_Angeles"}).isInDST === false; DateTime.fromISO("1974-06-01",{zone:"America/Los_Angeles"}).isInDST === true; DateTime.fromISO("1982-05-25T04:00:00Z",{zone:"America/Los_Angeles"}).isInDST === true; DateTime.fromISO("1982-01-25T04:00:00Z",{zone:"America/Los_Angeles"}).isInDST === false; a southern-hemisphere case such as DateTime.fromISO("2020-01-15",{zone:"Australia/Sydney"}).isInDST === true and DateTime.fromISO("2020-07-15",{zone:"Australia/Sydney"}).isInDST === false; DateTime.utc().isInDST === false; DateTime.invalid("because").isInDST is falsy.
4. Re-run the full test suite and compare failures to the baseline.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: do NOT modify or delete any existing test file; do not break any pre-existing passing test; do not add features. Report back: the root cause, the exact diff, before/after test failures, and verification output.

Repository: /luxon — the JavaScript library 'luxon' v1.20.0. Source in /luxon/src, tests in /luxon/test, jest (run `cd /luxon && npx jest`). Fix this reported bug:

BUG: `Duration.fromObject(...).normalize().toObject()` produces NaN for some unit combinations instead of folding smaller units into larger ones.
```js
Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 2 }).normalize().toObject()
// => { years: NaN }   (expected something numeric, e.g. { years: 1.5 })

Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 2 }).normalize().toObject()
// => { quarters: NaN } (expected something numeric)
```
No error or warning is raised; the user expects the smaller units folded into the larger unit so the result stays numeric.

Your task:
1. First run the full test suite to record pre-existing failures: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -60`. (Known pre-existing failures: 2 tests in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js about French locale hour padding — ignore those.)
2. Investigate /luxon/src/duration.js (`normalize`, `normalizeValues`, the conversion matrices) and /luxon/src/impl/conversions.js. Find the root cause (likely a missing/incorrect entry in the conversion matrix or in the unit ordering used by normalizeValues, causing a divide by undefined -> NaN). Fix it minimally.
3. Verify with a scratch script (write /luxon/scratch_check_dur.js, run `cd /luxon && npx babel-node scratch_check_dur.js`, then DELETE it). Check at least: the two cases above are numeric and correct; `Duration.fromObject({years:1,quarters:2}).normalize().toObject()` equals `{years:1.5}`; `Duration.fromObject({quarters:1,seconds:2}).normalize().toObject()` equals `{quarters:1}` (2 seconds fold into nothing at quarter granularity -> should be 1 quarter, not NaN); also test other combos: {months:1,weeks:2}, {years:1,months:14}, {days:1,hours:30}, {hours:1,minutes:90}, {quarters:5}, {weeks:1,days:8}, and confirm no NaN appears. Also confirm existing normalize tests still pass (`npx jest test/duration`).
